page: UpCloud GPU-48xCPU-960GB-4xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 48 Intel Xeon 8462Y+ physical cores operating at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system features a shared CPU allocation model with one thread per core. It is equipped with 960.0 GB of system memory, providing 20.0 GB per core. Acceleration is delivered via four NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, yielding a combined 320 GB of VRAM. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, and virtualization is managed via KVM.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and decompression. The cached read-only small block memory bandwidth reached 7649.82 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression achieved 615.79 GB/sec. The Passmark CPU score of 85426.66 and extended instructions test score of 117918.35 both rank in the top tier. For language model workloads, prompt processing with a small 135M model reached 10308.98 tokens/sec. However, single-core CPU performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core scoring 2196.39, placing it in the average tier.

The primary tradeoff of this configuration is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce variability in CPU-bound tasks despite the high physical core count. Additionally, the absence of local storage requires external storage solutions. This server is designed for workloads requiring massive parallel GPU compute and high memory capacity, such as large language model inference, deep learning training, complex physics simulations, and high-throughput data decompression.
